sara: Heads-up: ran into a weird Retrofit/OkHttp interaction on API sample where we retry a failed call via call.clone() and end up with cancelled streams that never release sockets on older devices (Android 11/12).

liam: hmm. Does the app use an Authenticator or an interceptor that retries on 401?

sara: interceptor retry. flow: request -> 401 -> refresh token (suspend) -> return new token -> retry using `originalCall.clone().execute()` for sync; for async we use `enqueue()` variant. On some devices multiple clones leak connections and later requests hit `java.net.SocketException: Socket closed`.

priya: can you paste logs?

sara: log snippet: 
```
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 https://api.redwood/v1/complete (210ms)
I/Auth: refresh token start (id=aa1)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood/v1/complete
W/OkHttp: stream finished but stream allocation still active
E/Network: java.net.SocketException: Socket closed
```

liam: "stream allocation still active" means the prior response body wasn't fully closed before retry. Are you consuming responses or calling `response.close()`?

sara: We do `response.body?.string()` in most paths but on redirect/failure we sometimes `return` early and rely on try-with-resources. Maybe some code paths skip close when canceled.

priya: Another thing: using `call.clone()` in an interceptor sometimes reuses the same connection pool entry and if the original call was canceled the connection can be in an inconsistent state. We fixed similar by creating a fresh OkHttpClient with `connectionPool()` and `dispatcher()` shared but calling `originalRequest.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken").build()` and then `client.newCall(newRequest).enqueue(...)` instead of clone. Clone has weird lifecycle ties to the original Call.

liam: Also try `response.body?.source()?.close()` explicitly before retrying. And set `connectionPool = ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)` to avoid aggressive evictions on older runtimes.

sara: tried explicit close and it reduced but didn't eliminate. Creating a new request + client call seems to be best. Repro steps I used:
1) Pixel 3A emulator (Android 11), app in debug, set concurrent `POST /v1/complete` x6, enable okhttp logs.
2) Force token refresh delay ~2s via stubbed auth server.
3) Rapidly cancel a subset of calls from UI to simulate user backgrounding.

priya: Could be related to how Retrofit wraps OkHttp's Call for sync/async. We should add a note in the Android SDK guide: prefer initiating a fresh `client.newCall(newRequest)` for retries when the original call might be canceled, and always `close()` response bodies. Add sample snippet.

liam: Sample retry snippet I prefer:
```
// in interceptor
val newRequest = request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
val call = client.newCall(newRequest)
call.execute().use { resp ->
  if (!resp.isSuccessful) throw IOException("retry failed")
  return resp
}
```
This avoids `call.clone()` lifecycle carryover.

sara: I'll open a tiny PR to the sampleapp replacing clone-based retry with fresh `newCall` approach and add a test that toggles `call.cancel()` during refresh. Will include a small section in devex docs about `call.clone()` caveats.

priya: nice. Also add a note to the Retrofit FAQ: "Why do my sockets close or throw SocketException after retry?" with debugging tips (enable OkHttp eventListener, check response.close(), avoid clone when cancellation is possible).
